items.title: Billie Pierce, De De Pierce, Israel Gorman, Joseph "Kid Twat" Butler Interview, 1963-11-20
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...Who were they? Uh, Papa Celestan. Buddy Petit. Chris Kelly. ... Most all of the New Orleans bands used to play over there.

ctx.x: Oh, yeah. We just lived together. Bill Rossman. Yeah, we're watching.

Yeah, actually, for all the nice boys and David Wyckoff, they were the ones who put up the money for the kids, I remember now. Let's see. Maybe I can get you to turn it off for a minute now, okay? Off. Time to start off. I don't know. Oh, no, I haven't been to Florida. Have you been to Florida? Where are you from? I'm from Florida. What part? Pensacola. Pensacola? Yeah. Can I embarrass you? What's your age? Now, what year were you born in? 1970. Born in 1970 over there? And what's your exact birthday? June the…

See? What are they calling you now? It's from the Boudoir. It has to be from the Boudoir. That's my handle. That's the handle you put on that. Well, the Boudoir, you see, I'm going to show you a lot of people don't know what a Boudoir is. You see, when I came down here from Memphis, you see, and I was cigarette test up there, and you go in there and smoke and test them cigarettes. That's what you call a Boudoir. What kind of cigarettes?

items.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-04-02
items.q: when you came and played with Buddy Petit and heard some of the New Orleans bands

ctx.x: She quit. Yeah, she's playing in bands. She's playing in different bands like I was, see. And then, let's see. Nice band. Then another fella, he's there now, Joe Jesse. He was a trumpet player. He's from out of my hometown out of Florida. Yes. He was a great trumpet player. And also, a drummer called Teddy Bear in my hometown. Teddy Bear. He's, oh, he's there now, I guess. I'm not sure he's there now. There was, uh, the Douglas, Douglas, uh, Butts of Douglas. They had an orchestra. Big band. That's in Florida,…

Mm-hmm. Well, can you tell us how did those bands compare with the, uh, well, when you came and played with Buddy Petit and heard some of the New Orleans bands, did they sound a good idea like the Florida bands or did they have a different swing to it? How did they sound?

Well, they all sounded all right to me. The same identical music because we saw swinging music, but the idea, just different faces. Yeah. It's different, you know, like a stranger come in. Well, she sure can play, he sure can play. That's it. Like it is right now. The music was the same, it's identical thing to me right then. You know, cause now, this Bebop stuff, I don't care, I don't use that, understand? But I'm just saying, well, that day, people was playing jazz. Yeah. Jazz, see, piano jazz, all that stuff.

items.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-10-07
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Well, anyway, after you left Buddy Petit and those guys, you went back to Birmingham... [INTERVIEWEE] Well, I stayed there with them about...

ctx.x: Buddy Manaday. I called him Buddy Manaday from Manderville. He stayed in Manderville. He played banjo. Yeah. Cause I went over there. Right. I'm telling you, he stayed over Manderville. Well, I'll tell you what happened. When Sadie got able to go back on the boat, where Buddy Manaday and Lawrence Tocco came to see the house of Sadie living on Allen. That's when I was here. And, uh, they wanted Sadie or somebody to do a piano player, understand? So that's when Lawrence and Manaday came over there, and Sadie and I…
Well, anyway, after you left Buddy Petit and those guys, you went back to Birmingham, you said, with the Nighthaw. Yeah. How long did you stay there?
Well, I stayed there with them about...
